paragraphs: Ahab did everything he could to dodge his ending. He put on a disguise, he sent another king out in the royal robes, and he tried to hide in the crowd. Then one man drew his bow "without taking special aim," and the arrow struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor (1 Kings 22:34). Friend, you can plan, you can disguise, you can dodge, but you cannot out-sneak the LORD.

Look at how the passage ends. The dogs licked up Ahab's blood "according to the word that the LORD had spoken" (1 Kings 22:38). I think that's the whole point. Ahab locked up the prophet Micaiah and acted like the LORD's word was just somebody's opinion, but the LORD's word did not need Ahab's permission to come true.

So here's what I bake into you today. When God says something, it stands, whether the king believes it or not. That's good news for a baker, because every promise in this Book stands the same way. Ahab's story is over, but the teaching isn't, so keep your oven warm and keep trusting the Word.
